title: From Powers of Two to Every n
content: The parent proves π(2^k) ≥ k, a bound only along the sparse powers of two. This file upgrades it to π(n) ≥ ⌊log₂ n⌋ at every natural number, using only monotonicity of π and 2^⌊log₂ n⌋ ≤ n. It is honestly weaker than the gallery's Chebyshev bound π(n) = Θ(n/log n); its value is being fully elementary and pointwise.
mathContext: The upgrade is pure bookkeeping: no new number theory beyond the parent's Bertrand-based bound is required.

title: primeCounting_ge_log2: π(n) ≥ ⌊log₂ n⌋
content: For n ≥ 1, set k = ⌊log₂ n⌋. Nat.pow_log_le_self gives 2^k ≤ n, so Nat.monotone_primeCounting gives π(2^k) ≤ π(n), and the parent's primeCounting_two_pow_ge gives k ≤ π(2^k). Chaining yields ⌊log₂ n⌋ ≤ π(n). The n = 0 case is simp.
mathContext: Transporting a bound known at 2^k to all n via monotonicity of a monotone counting function.

title: The Dual: pₖ ≤ 2^(k+1)
content: The counting bound has a dual bounding the size of the k-th prime, pₖ ≤ 2^(k+1), already formalized in PrimeGapBounds by iterating Bertrand's pₖ₊₁ ≤ 2·pₖ. It is re-exported here and read in log scale as ⌊log₂ pₖ⌋ ≤ k + 1, so both elementary directions of the Bertrand bridge sit side by side.
mathContext: Iterating Bertrand from below bounds the count of primes; iterating from p₀ = 2 bounds the primes themselves.

title: Explicit Prime-Count Certificates
content: π(8) ≥ 3 and π(1000) ≥ 9, obtained by evaluating ⌊log₂ 8⌋ = 3 and ⌊log₂ 1000⌋ = 9 with Nat.log_eq_of_pow_le_of_lt_pow and feeding them to the main bound — elementary certificates that there are at least 3 primes below 8 and at least 9 below 1000.
